title: Molecular Docking Analysis Of Heparin-Diclofenac Complexes: Insights Into Enhanced Cox Enzyme Inhibition For Pain Management
content: The aim of this study is to investigate the molecular interactions of heparin, diclofenac, and their complexes with cyclooxygenase enzymes (COX-1 and COX-2) using computational docking techniques. Molecular modeling and docking simulations were performed with HyperChem and HEX software, utilizing receptor structures from the Protein Data Bank (PDB). Binding energies and lipophilicity (logP) values were analyzed to evaluate the interaction strength and hydrophobic properties of the complexes compared to the individual drugs. The results demonstrated that both the heparin-diclofenac and diclofenac-heparin complexes exhibit stronger binding affinities to COX-1 and COX-2 than the drugs alone. Notably, the heparin-diclofenac complex showed the strongest binding, sug-gesting that molecular orientation significantly influences interaction efficiency. Further-more, differences in binding behavior between COX-1 and COX-2 were observed, likely due to structural variations in their active sites, with COX-2 providing a more favorable environment for complex interactions. The analysis also highlighted the impact of lipophilicity on binding properties, emphasizing the relevance of physicochemical characteristics in drug-receptor dynamics. These findings suggest that the formation of heparin-diclofenac complexes may enhance COX inhibition, presenting a potential strategy for developing more effective pain management therapies.
